key_insight: A graph neural network can learn method-dependent energy residuals to align heterogeneous DFT formation energies onto a common r2SCAN scale.
engineering_relevance: This makes it possible to merge legacy PBE datasets with higher-accuracy r2SCAN data for more reliable materials screening, phase stability, and battery design.
method: Train on 380,190 paired PBE–r2SCAN structures from MatPES.
Use a structure-aware GPTFF graph neural network to predict cross-functional energy residuals.
Convert PBE energies to r2SCAN-equivalent energies for dataset harmonization.
evidence_signal: The model achieves 14.3 meV/atom MAE on conversion, improving over CHGNet at 18.2 meV/atom; the abstract notes an average 107 meV/atom PBE–r2SCAN discrepancy in MatPES.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of paired training data, so extrapolation to unseen functionals, pseudopotentials, or chemistry may be less reliable.
paper_title: Aligning Heterogeneous DFT Datasets: A Graph Neural Network Approach to Cross-Functional Formation Energies
